answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks through proof-of-burn registration. Each participant permanently burns tokens to produce an ember proof, minting a non-transferable identity relic within a shared state lagoon. This forces attackers to incur an unrecoverable capital loss and token-acquisition cost per identity, preventing zero-cost replication. However, burning permanently locks out resource-poor autonomous agents and cannot stop well-funded entities from absorbing the destruction cost.
